correctness.rationale: The exact vertices are verified from the primary paper. An orthogonal Gaussian leaf-coordinate transform yields the pointwise two-branch maximum and conditional CDF. Signed exchangeability gives uniform exposures inside each of two vertex orbits, hence exact power sums for all collision orders. Gaussian upper/lower tail estimates prove both maxima approach sqrt(2 log m) in L2. The max Lipschitz bound leaves the shared hub coordinate as 2|Z| in the Gaussian width. Orthogonal projection to the zero-sum direction space, radial chi independence, fourth inverse-radius moments and Gaussian-max fourth moments justify the intrinsic sphere limit in L2 and its mean/variance. The included standalone checker passed 3,600 deterministic support/width comparisons and 12 numerical CDF diagnostics. No finite sample is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: A canonical family with 3m source vertices and exponentially many facets has a geometric normal-cone law not encoded by vertex/facet counts, the common vertex shell, facet tangency, or vertex covariance. Despite two different orbit cardinalities, the angular mass divides equally asymptotically; this forces an exact 9/8 collision inflation versus uniform exposure. Shared hub dependence causes order-one half-normal directional-width fluctuations instead of the usual Gumbel-scale residual Gaussian maxima. These are motivated structural facts for an infinite natural graph-polytope family, beyond a routine finite enumeration.
